result.title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?
result.summary: Looping re-applies a block of layers so that each token passes through the block more than once. Adding a loop to a trained model is attractive because it leaves the parameter count, and hence the disk size, the memory footprint and the training cost unchanged. Unfortunately, every generated token pays for the loop. Re-applying m of N layers makes each token about (N+m)/N times as expensive. Loops that a model learns during large-scale pretraining justify this price, but whether loops added after pretraining justify this cost remains unclear. We compare a looped model with two simple baselines. We first compare it with the same model trained identically without the loop (equal parameters). Secondly, we compare it with the best unlooped use of the same inference floating-point operations (equal FLOPs). Across Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B parameters, only the looped 0.8B model beats both baselines. At 4B and 9B, the looped model does not beat the first baseline, i.e. the same model trained without the loop. This is not because the benchmarks are too easy, since on the same benchmarks the unlooped 9B model still scores up to 13 points higher than the 4B model, showing that there is ample room for improvement. Introducing loops in an already pretrained model therefore only pays for small models with a fixed parameter budget.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在预训练后的 Qwen3 系列模型上重新应用部分层形成循环，并与等参数无循环模型及等 FLOPs 的最优无循环基线比较，检验额外推理计算是否值得。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中「循环层—等 FLOPs 对照—规模依赖收益」的负结果可供核查 loop 式 latent reasoning 的计算成本与收益分配，尤其提示大模型后加循环可能不划算；但研究为纯文本，视觉证据与状态内容未涉及。
